newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Feb industrial production seen strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Feb industrial production seen strong.

text.p: February industrial production and capacity utilization data due on Friday were expected to show continuing strength in the manufacturing sector of the U.S. economy.

Economists polled by Reuters expected, on average, industrial production would pick up 0.5 percent from an unchanged figure in January and that capacity utilization would rise to 83.5 percent from January's 83.3 percent. The data were scheduled for release by the Federal Reserve at 915 EST/1415 GMT Friday.

The basic trend in manufacturing is very good and there's every reason to expect further gains," said Charles Lieberman, director of financial markets research at Chase Securities Inc. Lieberman's expectations mirrored consensus estimates.

"Order backlogs are rising even excluding the aircraft and defense categories, incoming orders are growing strongly and the inventory-to-sales ratio is at a low level," Lieberman said. "On top of that consumer demand remains vigorous."
Despite the health seen in the manufacturing sector, Lieberman didn't expect the Fed to tighten at its March 25 meeting.
"It's a tough call, but my sense is the Fed probably leaves policy alone. Greenspan is confident that when the Fed moves policy next it will be a tightening," he said.
Lieberman said the Fed may want to see more data for 1997 before committing to a policy change.
Alan Levenson, money market economist at UBS Securities Inc. expected to see industrial production rise by 0.7 percent and capacity utilization to increase to 83.7 percent.
"We'll see a good rebound from a depressed reading in January that was all weather-related," Levenson said.
Jerry Zukowski, economist at PaineWebber Inc., agreed a weather-related rebound should occur.
"It will difficult to see how much of this is fundamental. The entire manufacturing sector continues to grow moderately," Zukowski said.
Zukowski expected a 0.4 percent rise in industrial production and capacity utilization of 83.4 percent.
"This is not a number that affects the Fed" in policy deliberations, Zukowski said. "It's neutral in terms of Fed policy."
